data.title: PB Fintech shares fall up to 6% after co-founder Alok Bansal to step down from executive role next year
data.description:
Shares of PB Fintech Ltd. declined up to 6% on Thursday, November 19, as the the company's co-founder, executive vice-chairman Alok Bansal has decided to step down from his executive role. The stock has since recovered most of its losses.

PB Fintech, in an exchange filing on Wednesday, said Bansal's last day as executive vice-chairman and whole-time director and as key managerial personnel / senior management will be March 31, 2027.

Bansal will continue on the company's board as a non-executive, non-independent director from April 1, 2027, the company said.

The board of directors on Wednesday approved the change in designation, on the recommendation of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee. The same is subject to the approval of shareholders of the company.

Alok Bansal has stated the change is on account of his personal desire to step back from day-to-day executive responsibilities, according to the regulatory filing. He has confirmed there is no other material reason for the change.

The board placed on record its appreciation for Bansal's significance and contributions to the company over the past 18 years and his role in building and strengthening its businesses and leadership team, PB Fintech said.

The stock has since recovered from the lows of the day, and is now trading 2.1% lower at ₹1,014.3. Its intraday low of ₹970.4 was below its IPO price of ₹980.

data.title: The Iran War Could Permanently Slash Reliance on Hormuz, IEA Says
data.description:
By Giulia Petroni

Shipping disruptions due to the Iran war have shattered confidence in the Strait of Hormuz, spurring a costly overhaul of the global energy trade that could dramatically cut the world's dependence on the route over the next decade, the International Energy Agency said.

Before the conflict, around 20 million barrels of oil a day passed through Hormuz, a narrow waterway connecting the Persian Gulf to global markets. That could fall to 8.5 million barrels a day by 2030 and to less than 2 million by 2035 if the strait remains severely disrupted, the Paris-based agency said in its World Energy Outlook.

"The Hormuz crisis has delivered a huge shock to the system," IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol said. "I don't see any credible pathway for the energy world to return to the way it was before."

Still, the Middle East is set to remain the world's largest exporter of oil to international markets as major Gulf producers race to build alternative pipelines and routes.

Since the Iran war began in late February, Saudi Arabia has relied on its East-West pipeline to move crude toward the Red Sea, while the United Arab Emirates used its pipeline to the port of Fujairah on the Gulf of Oman.

Now, around 7 million barrels a day of new pipeline capacity is under construction or under consideration to help Gulf producers move oil without passing through the strait, the IEA said. Building the projects will require an estimated $40 billion of investment, adding about $2 to the cost of each barrel of Middle Eastern oil exported, the agency estimates.

"It is not easy, but the energy world could conceivably manage without the strait," Birol said. "It cannot manage without the Middle East."

Meanwhile, global oil prices have been volatile: Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, swung from around $71 a barrel prewar to peaks above $126, before falling back toward $93 a barrel in November.

The price reaction was less severe than the scale of the disruption might have suggested, coinciding with a time of ample global supply and well-stocked inventories.

The IEA now expects the global oil market to swing back into oversupply as Middle Eastern production recovers faster than global demand growth. From a surplus of 1.7 million barrels a day in the current quarter, the glut is set to widen further next year to about 3.8 million barrels a day.

Between March and October, global oil demand fell by around 3.7 million barrels a day from a year earlier, as higher prices, physical shortages, government-imposed measures and weaker economic activity curbed consumption.

The decline was particularly sharp in the Middle East, where demand dropped 10%, and Asia, where it fell 5%. China's seaborne crude imports fell to around 6 million barrels a day in June from 11.6 million in February as the country drew down inventories, restricted fuel exports and switched between fuels.

Over time, the IEA also expects the crisis to reinforce a broader shift toward countries' domestic energy sources. Renewables and nuclear energy will be the biggest beneficiaries, while energy-efficiency measures, biofuels and, in some Asian countries, coal could also gain ground.

"All in all, countries want to rely more and more on homegrown energy," Birol said.

Volatile fuel prices have reinforced the case for electrification. Global demand for electricity has grown faster than the world economy since 2019 and at twice the rate of overall energy demand, driven by electric vehicles, air conditioning, industrial motors, heat pumps and data centers. The IEA expects electricity demand to accelerate further through 2035, with electricity approaching 30% of final energy consumption across all scenarios.

In its World Energy Outlook, the IEA presents a series of possible scenarios rather than a single forecast.

Write to Giulia Petroni at giulia.petroni@wsj.com

data.title: Food & Life Companies' Earnings Set to Gain From Faster Store Openings, Strong Sales — Market Talk
data.description: Food & Life Companies' earnings stand to benefit from faster store openings in Japan and overseas and strong sales, SMBC Nikko Securities' Ryozo Minagawa says in a research report. The brokerage assumes 119 overseas store openings annually during the company's medium-term plan through the year ending September 2029. With a focus mostly in regions where the Japanese food-service holding company has a proven track record, the brokerage sees a strong likelihood of success. In Japan, the company is aiming for net store openings of around 25 a year, mainly in urban areas. The brokerage raises the stock's target price to 6,800 yen from Y6,100, with an unchanged neutral rating. Shares are 1.5% higher at Y6,334. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)

data.title: Japan's Meiko boosts Vietnam PCB plant investment to $800mn
data.description:
Japanese printed circuit board (PCB) manufacturer Meiko Electronics (6787) has added $450mn to its factory project in northern Vietnam, raising total investment in the plant to $800mn.

According to The Investor, Meiko (6787), which started establishing itself in Vietnam close to two decades ago, is expanding that footprint with the larger budget, a move that coincides with rising global demand for sophisticated circuit boards found in high-end mobile phones, satellite communications equipment and servers for artificial intelligence.

Construction began in June on the factory, which subsidiary Meiko Hoa Binh Electronics operates in Phu Tho province's Bo Trai Song Da Industrial Park. Under the updated plan, the building will rise to five storeys instead of three, and its floor space will double from 60,000 sqm to 120,000 square metres.

The extra funds will lift yearly output in the second phase to 261,000 sqm, up from 180,000 sqm. Designed capacity will total 504,000 sqm per year once the site runs at full scale, which Meiko expects by the end of its 2026 fiscal year on March 31, 2027.

The factory makes high-frequency, high-density substrate-like PCBs and high density interconnect (HDI) boards. It started volume output of AI server boards in August 2026 and runs dedicated lines for a large US smartphone client. Meiko also plans to mass-produce optical transceiver components, which carry very fast data traffic inside AI data centres and cloud networks.

The company is spending more at its other Vietnamese sites as well. Planned capital expenditure at its fourth plant in Hanoi rose to JPY45bn ($282.25mn) from JPY25bn. The plant builds high-layer-count HDI boards for satellite and AI uses, along with memory module substrates. Spending at the Quang Minh plant in Hanoi increased to JPY50bn from JPY40bn.

Spending on the Yen Quang facility, also located in Phu Tho, is being doubled to JPY120bn from the previous JPY60bn, and the site's floor area will expand to 200,000 sqm. Its main customer base will be the satellite communications sector. Quang Minh and Yen Quang are both expected to be running at full scale during the latter half of fiscal 2027.

Meiko set up Meiko Electronics Vietnam in Hanoi in 2006. It opened an electronics assembly plant in 2008 and began making PCBs in 2010. Today it has more than 6,000 staff in the country.

In the fiscal year to March 31, 2026, Meiko Electronics Vietnam posted net sales of JPY113.64bn, an increase of 25.7% on the previous year. Net profit grew 32% to JPY9.71bn.

data.title: Musk: Jensen Huang irreplaceable, regrets midterm spend
data.description:
Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk likened Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia to kicking Michael Jordan off a team riding a winning streak, while expressing regret over how much he spent on the U.S. midterm elections.

“You’ve got a winning streak ... and then you kick Michael Jordan off your team,” Musk told during an interview at The New York Times’ DealBook Summit on Wednesday. He added, “Doesn’t seem like a smart decision to me.”

The SpaceX and Tesla chief executive, who previously said it would be an “honor” to hire the Nvidia co-founder, added that no one could really replace Huang. Musk said he had heard similar views about Huang’s departure from Nvidia, including from President Donald Trump.

“I think the president has voiced publicly that he thinks Jensen should have stayed as CEO, and everyone I know thinks the same ... this is, at the end of the day, the Nvidia board decision,” he said, adding, “We’re not on the board, right?”

Tesla has been one of Nvidia’s key customers, while Huang has frequently commended Musk’s AI ambitions, particularly Tesla’s autonomous driving technology, xAI, and its Optimus humanoid robot.

Asked about the midterms, Musk said he felt “pretty foolish” about spending at least $474M with little to show for it, though he added that “maybe it would have been much worse without that,” according to a CNBC report.

Musk said his goal had been to prevent the presidency, House, and Senate from all being controlled by one party. “If I could rewind the clock, I would have spent less money,” he added.

data.title: Why Did DIS, TGT, ASO Stocks Surge To 52-Week Highs Today?
data.description:
Key points:
  • Disney stock reached a 52-week high of $123.37 after Q4 revenue rose 16% to $25.9 billion.
  • Target stock hit a two-year high of $171.91 after its Q3 results beat Street expectations.
  • Academy Sports gained as its fiscal 2026 expansion is set to reach 23 new locations across 10 states. 

Walt Disney Co. (DIS), Target Corp. (TGT) and Academy Sports and Outdoors (ASO) stocks climbed to fresh 52-week highs on Wednesday as strong earnings, improving shopper traffic and ambitious store expansion fueled investor optimism.

Disney and Target stocks gained 4% each, while Academy Sports stock climbed 5%.

Disney’s Growth Makes Analysts Raise Price Targets

Walt Disney stock hit an annual high of $123.37 after the entertainment giant reported stronger-than-expected fiscal fourth-quarter (Q4) results across its Entertainment, Experiences and Sports businesses. Revenue climbed 16% year-on-year to $25.9 billion, while operating income increased 43% to $5 billion. Adjusted earnings reached $1.77 per share, beating analysts’ consensus estimate of $1.68.

The results evoked positive reactions from Wall Street, with Needham increasing its price target to $135 from $125 and Raymond James lifting its target to $133 from $119. Both firms maintained bullish ratings on the stock. Analysts also pointed to Disney's planned $3 billion in cost savings through fiscal 2029.

Disney+ and Hulu helped drive growth in the Entertainment division, which brought in $11.9 billion in revenue. Its Experiences business’s revenue was $10.1 billion, supported by more visitors to U.S. theme parks and higher customer spending.

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘extremely bullish’.

Target Benefits From Higher Store Traffic 

Target stock reached over a two-year high of $171.91 after the retailer exceeded Q3 Wall Street estimates and raised its full-year outlook. Revenue rose 7.1% to $27.1 billion. Adjusted earnings came in at $2.65 per share, compared with the $2.08 analyst consensus.

However, Target's earnings included a $0.50-per-share boost from tariff refunds. Without that benefit, adjusted EPS was $2.15. Comparable sales grew 5.6%, helped by a 5% rise in store traffic. The company now expects 2026 sales to grow about 6% and guided annual EPS to $10.65 to $11.40.

Retail sentiment around the stock improved to ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘bullish’.

Academy Sports Advances Its Store Expansion Plan

Academy Sports stock also climbed to a two-year high of $73.82 as the sporting goods retailer moved closer to completing its fiscal 2026 expansion program. The company is adding locations in regional markets as it looks to boost its physical retail presence.

Academy opened two new stores in Marshall and Magnolia, Texas, and plans to open another in Pascagoula, Mississippi, before the fiscal year ends. This will bring its 2026 total to 23 new stores across 10 states. Retail sentiment toward the stock remained ‘bullish’.

So far this year, DIS, TGT and ASO stocks have gained between 7% and 69%.

data.title: Hong Kong stocks hit 4-month low, as US-China tensions weigh on tech
data.description:
Hong Kong's benchmark stock index sank nearly 2% to hit four-month lows while China shares sagged further, as fresh trade tensions flared up between the US and China despite symbolic meetings between Xi Jinping and Donald Trump in the Chinese tech hub of Shenzhen.

** Risk appetite is also curbed by the prospect of further US rate hikes that will likely tighten global liquidity.

** Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index was down 1.9% by the lunch break, plumbing the lowest level since late June. The Hang Seng Tech Index hit a 26-month low.

** In China, both the blue-chip CSI300 Index and the Shanghai Composite Index fell roughly 0.4%, touching the lowest in more than a year.

** Investors worry that the world's two largest economies are careening toward a fresh tit-for-tat trade war spiral, after Republicans' defeat in the US midterm election appears to have prompted the White House to take a more hawkish policy against China.

** The Nvidia saga has already led to tighter controls over advanced chip exports and other measures to slow China's progress in AI.

** Sources told Reuters that the Trump administration is considering requiring US companies to publicly disclose their use of Chinese AI models in a bid to discourage reliance on the technology. Meanwhile, a US House panel asked Microsoft on Wednesday to brief lawmakers on a report which said the company could allow the Chinese firm ByteDance to use OpenAI models through Microsoft's Azure cloud platform.

** Hong Kong-listed AI model developers and AI hyperscalers, whose competitiveness depends on advanced computing power, tumbled on Thursday.

** Minimax slumped 8% to record lows while Z.AI tumbled 6%.

** Tencent dropped nearly 7% to more than two-year lows after its third-quarter revenue missed forecasts, and the company said new US chip curbs may slow model training.

** In China, tech stocks in areas that rely on advanced chips, including cloud computing (.CSI931469), artificial intelligence and big data , led the declines.

data.title: Indian shares edge higher despite Asia selloff; IT caps gains
data.description:
By Bharath Rajeswaran and Vivek Kumar M

Indian shares defied a selloff in Asian markets on Thursday, led by auto and financial stocks, although weakness in IT shares, following hawkish signals from the Federal Reserve, capped gains.

The Nifty 50 rose 0.20% to 25,280.05 and the Sensex gained 0.19% to 82,194.23 as of 10:38 a.m. IST.

MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan (.MISX00000PUS) fell about 1.9%, as continued selling in AI-linked stocks and hawkish signals from the Fed weighed on sentiment.

While the Nifty faced "profit-taking in the previous session, the broader bullish structure remains intact," said Sudeep Shah, head of technical and derivatives research at SBI Securities.

"On the upside, 25,370-25,400 remains the immediate hurdle and a sustained breakout above this zone could signal a resumption of the uptrend towards 25,600."

Thirteen of 16 major sectors advanced, while the broader small-cap and mid-cap indexes added about 0.1% and 0.4%, respectively.

The auto index climbed 3.3%, supported by resilient vehicle demand after the festive season and lower crude and metal prices, which eased input cost pressures.

Banks gained 0.6% and state-owned lenders rose 2%, extending a November rally underpinned by foreign buying, steady earnings and attractive valuations.

Financials, oil and gas, and auto stocks have risen 10%-18.5% this month, helping drive the benchmark indexes about 10% higher.

Meanwhile, minutes from the Fed's October meeting showed that policymakers saw a need to intensify efforts to curb inflation, though they agreed to hold interest rates steady for now.

IT stocks fell 2.1% as the prospect of higher US rates renewed concerns about client technology spending, according to analysts. Indian IT companies derive a significant share of revenue from the United States.

Among stocks, online-payment firms Paytm , One Mobikwik and Pine Labs fell 6%, 6.7% and 4.3%, respectively, following reports of a potential delay in the government's rollout of the merchant discount rate.

data.title: Piramal Pharma to acquire remaining 26% stake in Yapan Bio
data.description:
Piramal Pharma Limited said it would acquire the remaining 26 per cent equity stake in Yapan Bio Private Limited, a subsidiary of the company, from its existing shareholders.

The administrative committee authorised by Piramal Pharma’s board of directors has “approved the exercise of the company’s call option to acquire the balance 26 per cent equity stake in Yapan Bio Private Limited,” the drugmaker said in an announcement to the stock exchange.

Acquisition terms yet to be finalised

The final terms of the acquisition, including the acquisition consideration and the effective date of transfer of shares, are yet to be finalised, it added.

“Consequent to the exercise of the call option, the company is engaged in discussions with the shareholders of Yapan in relation to matters necessary for consummation of the proposed transaction,” it said.

Yapan to become a wholly owned subsidiary

Yapan is a contract development and manufacturing organisation focused on services for vaccines and biologics. After the proposed transaction is completed, Piramal Pharma’s shareholding in Yapan is expected to increase from the present 74 per cent to 100 per cent, making it a wholly owned subsidiary, it said.

data.title: Nifty opens below 25,200; IT bleeds as Fed jitters, Anthropic IPO reshape market mood
data.description:
Benchmark indices slipped on Thursday morning, extending Wednesday’s losses, as hawkish signals from the minutes of the United States Federal Reserve meeting and a stronger dollar dampened global risk appetite. The Nifty 50 opened at 25,186.80 against a previous close of 25,227.95, and was trading at 25,149.85, down 78.10 points or 0.31 per cent, as of 9.27 am. The Sensex opened at 82,074.16 against a previous close of 82,031.81 and fell to 81,802.00, shedding 229.81 points or 0.28 per cent.

Wednesday’s session had already seen the Nifty shed 159.45 points, or 0.63 per cent, closing at 25,227.95. The broader market also weakened, with the Nifty Midcap 100 falling 1.22 per cent and the Nifty Smallcap 100 declining 0.35 per cent. The BSE advance-decline ratio slumped to 0.52, reflecting broad-based selling pressure.

  • Read: Stocks to watch, Nov 19: Jio Financial, Bharat Forge, LT Foods, National Aluminium, Dalmia Bharat
IT stocks lead losses; rupee appreciation adds pressure

Information technology stocks were the sharpest drag on Thursday morning. Infosys fell 2.49 per cent to ₹1,081.20 against a previous close of ₹1,108.80. Tech Mahindra declined 1.71 per cent to ₹1,720.00 from ₹1,750.00, and HCL Technologies lost 1.70 per cent to ₹1,321.80 from ₹1,344.70. The rupee’s continued appreciation to 93.44 against the dollar, a seven-month high, has added pressure on export-sensitive IT earnings.

  • Read also: Anthropic prices IPO at $83, beating target range in blockbuster AI listing

Titan fell 2.08 per cent to ₹4,551.40 from a previous close of ₹4,648.10, while Eternal dropped 2.04 per cent to ₹358.55 from ₹366.00. Wednesday had already seen the Consumer sector decline 3.10 per cent and Metal stocks fall 2.45 per cent.

Maruti Suzuki, Eicher Motors among top gainers

On the gainers’ side, Maruti Suzuki rose 2.72 per cent to ₹12,975.00 from an open of ₹12,632.00, the top Nifty performer. Eicher Motors advanced 1.99 per cent to ₹7,853.00. IndiGo gained 1.26 per cent to ₹5,568.80 from ₹5,499.40, Hindustan Unilever added 1.08 per cent to ₹2,014.50 from ₹1,981.40, and Tata Motors (TMPV) edged up 1.07 per cent to ₹255.25 from ₹252.90.

FII buying continues for seventh consecutive session

Foreign institutional investors extended their buying streak to a seventh consecutive session on Wednesday, recording net equity purchases of ₹5,866 crore. FII inflows for the month have reached ₹94,299 crore. Domestic institutional investors, however, turned net sellers, with outflows of ₹3,159 crore. Vijayakumar of Geojit Investments noted that “...the sustained inflows from FIIs, which have touched a record ₹94,299 crores so far this month, assisted by impressive earnings growth, have the potential to take the market forward...”

He also flagged a structural shift: “...the undervalued large-caps are witnessing a catch-up in valuations while the broader market is seeing overvaluations coming down...”

Hawkish Fed minutes lift dollar; gold and silver slide

The October FOMC minutes showed policymakers open to rate hikes larger than 25 basis points if inflation remained unfavourable. The US Dollar Index rose to 103.81. The 10-year US Treasury yield eased marginally to 5.06 per cent from 5.10 per cent.

Gold bore the brunt, with spot prices falling 3.2 per cent to $3,726.19 per ounce and MCX December gold at ₹1,29,880 per 10 grams. Silver declined 5 per cent to $45.03 per ounce internationally, with MCX silver at ₹1,60,949 per kg. Vikram Subburaj of Giottus cautioned that “...investors should avoid trying to catch the bottom during a rapid correction. Staggered buying, measured exposure and clear risk limits are more appropriate until global prices and interest-rate expectations stabilise...”

WTI crude slipped to $82 per barrel and Brent to around $92 per barrel on rising US inventories.

Wall Street mixed; Nvidia falls, Anthropic prices IPO

Wall Street ended mixed overnight. The Dow fell 561 points, or 1.11 per cent, to 50,198, its fifth consecutive daily decline. The S&P 500 slipped 0.23 per cent to 7,323, while the Nasdaq rose 0.42 per cent to 24,429. Nvidia fell 2.9 per cent, now down 36.9 per cent from its October 6 peak, as markets absorbed the news that the company’s board does not plan to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO.

Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share, valuing the AI company at $1.5 trillion. It will trade on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT. Vikram Kasat of PL Capital noted that “...Anthropic, which will trade on the Nasdaq under ticker symbol ANT, will be the first place investors look to check the health of the tech market...”

Shrikant Chouhan of Kotak Neo said that “...for day traders, 25,400/82,500 will act as the immediate resistance zone. As long as the market trades below these levels, weak sentiment is likely to persist, with the possibility of a retest of 25,050–25,000/81,500–81,300...”

Asian markets open lower

Asian markets opened weaker, with the Hang Seng down 1.5 per cent, South Korea’s Kospi down more than 1 per cent, and Japan’s Nikkei 225 marginally lower.

data.title: Refex Industries wins pond ash contract in India
data.description:
Indian company Refex Industries (BSE: 532884) has secured a pond ash utilisation contract worth up to INR280mn ($2.995mn), the company told the Bombay Stock Exchange and the National Stock Exchange of India in a filing on November 17.

The award came from a domestic client that the company described only as a major power producer. The deal will run for two years, and the INR280mn figure is a cumulative ceiling that excludes taxes and duties. According to the filing, Refex will supply goods and services connected with the use of pond ash. The company did not identify the power producer or give further commercial terms.

Refex said neither its promoter, its promoter group nor any of its group companies holds an interest in the entity that granted the contract. The company also stated that the agreement does not count as a related party transaction. The disclosure was made under Regulation 30 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India's listing obligations and disclosure rules, read with a regulatory master circular dated January 30, 2026.

Pond ash is used as a containment material for the waste created by the combustion of fossil fuels at power generation facilities.

data.title: Anthropic’s rise to $1.5 trillion puts Indian companies’ competitiveness in focus: Uday Kotak
data.description:
Indian companies may be undervalued or need to catch up with the changing global economic landscape, said Uday Kotak, Founder and Director of Kotak Mahindra Bank, highlighting the gap between the valuations of global artificial intelligence companies and India’s largest businesses.

In a post on X, Kotak pointed to Anthropic, the US-based company behind AI chatbot Claude, which he said had reached a valuation of USD 1.5 trillion within around five years of its establishment.

He noted that this was higher than the combined market capitalisation of India’s top 10 companies.

“Anthropic, an AI company known for Claude, listed at a valuation of $ 1.5 trillion. It did not exist till ~ 5 years ago. This is more than the combined market cap of the top 10 Indian companies,” Kotak said.

  • Read also: Anthropic prices IPO at $83, beating target range in blockbuster AI listing

He further questioned India’s position in the emerging business landscape, asking, “Are we undervalued, or do we need to catch up in the new world? Or both?”

Anthropic IPO values AI company at $1.5 trillion

Kotak’s remarks came as Anthropic priced its initial public offering (IPO) at USD 83 per share, above its earlier expected range of USD 70-78. The company’s shares are scheduled to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on Thursday under the ticker symbol ‘ANT’.

According to the company’s announcement, the offering comprises 980 million shares, including 956.35 million shares being sold by Anthropic and 23.65 million by existing shareholders. The offering is expected to close on November 20, subject to customary conditions.

The IPO price places Anthropic’s valuation above the USD 1.4 trillion level it had previously targeted. The final market capitalisation will depend on the total number of shares outstanding.

Anthropic’s AI business and global ambitions

Founded in 2021, Anthropic develops the Claude family of AI models and has expanded its business around artificial intelligence tools, including coding applications.

The company’s public listing comes amid growing investor interest in AI businesses and highlights the scale of valuations being commanded by companies in the sector. Kotak’s observation brings attention to the challenge for Indian businesses to build and scale globally competitive companies as AI reshapes the business landscape.

data.title: Binance hackers stole 192 tokens across 11 networks, court docs show
data.description:
Hackers behind the record $6.3 billion Binance hack stole a total of 192 cryptocurrencies across 11 blockchain networks, new court documents reveal.

The figures come from an asset schedule submitted by Nest Clearing and Custody Limited, which operated the affected Binance wallets, and included in a Wednesday Abu Dhabi court order shared with Cointelegraph.

Tether’s USDt (USDT) accounted for the largest share of stolen value at $2.50 billion, followed by $1.42 billion in Bitcoin (BTC) and $826 million in Circle’s USDC (USDC). Together, the three assets made up about 76% of the total value of misappropriated tokens.

While earlier reports identified many of the tokens stolen in the attack, the latest court documents show a full breakdown of all crypto assets stolen in the attack, including the quantities and what they were worth at the time of the theft.

Cointelegraph’s analysis found that fiat-linked stablecoins accounted for at least $3.46 billion, 55% of the assets stolen. Beyond USDt and USDC, the court schedule lists nine other fiat-linked stablecoins.

These included Ripple USD (RLUSD), World Liberty Financial USD (USD1), Ethena USDe (USDE), First Digital USD (FDUSD), Sky Dollar (USDS), StraitsX USD (XUSD), Binance USD (BUSD), Pax Dollar (USDP) and Eurite (EURI). The nine stablecoins were worth $132.4 million combined at the time of the theft.

Stolen memecoins, gold-backed tokens

The Binance hackers also stole $37.9 million in memecoins, led by $34.9 million in Pepe and $2.3 million in Shiba Inu (SHIB).

Another $58 million in tokenized gold and more than $5 million across five gaming and metaverse tokens, including The Sandbox (SAND), Axie Infinity (AXS) and Decentraland (MANA), were stolen in the hack. Around $73.5 million of Wrapped Beacon ETH (WBETH) was stolen.

The haul also included $97.4 million across three DeFi tokens, led by $45.1 million in Uniswap’s UNI, followed by $37.3 million in Ethena’s ENA and $15.1 million in Aave’s AAVE.

Meanwhile, Ethereum accounted for roughly 60% of the stolen assets by value, more than any other blockchain network.

Abu Dhabi court to hear bid for frozen assets on Dec. 1

Cointelegraph previously reported that the Abu Dhabi Global Market Courts issued a $6.5 billion worldwide freezing injunction against the unidentified people accused of carrying out the attack.

The order restricts them from dealing with assets up to that value and requires them to disclose worldwide assets worth more than $50,000 in sworn statements by Nov. 30.

A separate order requires 18 named firms, including Circle and BitGo Bank & Trust, to maintain existing freezes on assets linked to the hack.

Court documents show it will consider on Dec. 1 whether to extend that injunction and whether the firms must hand over the assets they froze.

The US Department of Justice said last Thursday it had obtained court authorization to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion of the $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency stolen from Binance.

The authorization covers part of the more than $2.7 billion in stolen assets that US authorities and private-sector partners have frozen since the Oct. 29 hack. Investigators are still working to recover additional funds.

data.title: Elon Musk Names 2 Anthropic Favorites Ahead Of Its IPO — Flags A Risk To 10-GW Opportunity For SpaceX
data.description:
Key points:
  • Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share, raising $81.3 billion and surpassing SpaceX’s June offering as the largest on record.
  • Musk said Anthropic told him it was likely to keep renting computing power from SpaceX and could want another 10 gigawatts.
  • Musk said he would end the contracts if he believed Anthropic was doing something “really terrible for the world.”

On the eve of Anthropic’s Nasdaq debut, Elon Musk praised its Opus and Fable models and said that the Claude maker could want another 10 gigawatts of computing power from SpaceX unless tighter limits on AI curbed that demand.

“They make a great AI. Opus and Fable are great products,” Musk told New York Times columnist Andrew Ross Sorkin at Wednesday’s DealBook Summit.

Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share, above its $70 to $78 target range. The $81.3 billion offering surpassed SpaceX’s June IPO as the largest on record, with Anthropic expected to begin trading Thursday on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT.

Meanwhile, SPCX shares closed Wednesday at $143.50, up 6% from their June IPO price of $135.

Elon Musk’s OpenAI Ties To Anthropic

Sorkin opened by recalling Musk’s prediction that some newer cloud providers would struggle to make money. Then he turned to an apparent contradiction in Musk’s own business: SpaceX was renting computing power to a company Musk had once criticized as a threat to Western civilization.

Musk said he met with Anthropic employees before going ahead with the deal. Some were people he already knew. “Yeah, by the way, before we rented them any compute, I went and met with a lot of people at Anthropic,” he said. “And it turns out I actually do know a lot of people at Anthropic from my OpenAI days.”

He called the team diligent and said that its members seemed to care about the future. “My interaction so far with the Anthropic team is that they seem like good people and they seem principled,” Musk said. “I kind of like the guys.”

Anthropic Could Seek Another 10 GW From SpaceX

Sorkin said there had been speculation that Anthropic might end its SpaceX contracts and that the company had apparently raised the possibility with some investors. When asked whether he expected it to leave, Musk said his own conversations pointed the other way.

“I think that it’s unlikely that they will do so,” Musk said. “So when I talk to Anthropic, they tell me it is extremely likely that they will continue to rent compute from SpaceX. And in fact that they want significantly more.”

Musk said Anthropic still had to consider a worst-case scenario, in which severe limits on what AI systems could do would leave it unable to use the computing capacity. But the scenario Anthropic considered most likely, he said, involved a much bigger request.

“But they told me that their highest probability outcome is that they would like an incremental 10 gigawatts of compute from SpaceX,” Musk said. “So that’s a big number.”

For scale, 10 gigawatts is 10,000 megawatts. In May, Anthropic said its agreement to use SpaceX’s entire Colossus 1 data center would give it more than 300 megawatts of new capacity and access to over 220,000 Nvidia chips.

What Would Make Musk End Anthropic Contracts?

Musk made it clear that SpaceX could walk away, too. “And these are relatively short term deals that either party can terminate,” he said. “If I feel Anthropic is doing something really terrible for the world, obviously I would end those contracts.” He said Anthropic could also end the agreements with three to six months’ notice, depending on the contract.

Anthropic’s prospectus gives investors the written terms. The existing agreements with SpaceX’s AI unit cover spending of up to $120.5 billion through 2029. Anthropic expected payments to reach about $3.1 billion a month once all contracted capacity was delivered, which it anticipated in December. The agreements have initial periods ending in January and March 2027, respectively. After those dates, either side can cancel with 90 days’ written notice.

How Do Retail Traders Feel About ANT And SPCX?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment was ‘bullish’ on SPCX amid ‘normal’ message volume and ‘extremely bullish’ on Anthropic (ANT) amid ‘extremely high’ message volume.

One user said, “$ANT This might not go well tomorrow. The odds are much higher than with spacex. Market conditions were also far better back in June.”

View this Stocktwits post

Another user said, “$ANT We have two nice days of volatility and opportunity here. I’ll be scalping every chance I get. Once the options chain goes live, I know a lot of shorts will be rolling in.”

data.title: Gold holds near 14-month low as Fed hike bets weigh
data.description:
Key points:
  • Traders price in 90% chance of a 25-bp Fed hike in December
  • Global platinum market to swing back to deficit next year
  • Break below $3,800 risks reinforcing bearish sentiment- OCBC analysts

By Sukanya Mitra

Gold held steady on Thursday, hovering near a 14-month low as a stronger dollar and expectations of a US Federal Reserve interest rate hike weighed on bullion, with investors awaiting comments from central bank officials for fresh policy cues.

Spot gold was little changed at $3,722.84 per ounce by 0452 GMT, after hitting its lowest level since September 2025 at $3,693.13 per ounce earlier in the session. US gold futures for December delivery fell 0.5% to $3,723.90.

"We saw a little bit of a pop earlier today in the session after what was a very aggressive sell-off yesterday. But now, we're seeing selling pressure returning," said Ilya Spivak, head of global macro at Tastylive.

The US dollar hovered near a 19-month high, making greenback-priced bullion more expensive for buyers overseas.

Fed officials saw a growing risk last month that they might need to intensify their efforts to control inflation, even as they agreed to keep interest rates steady for the moment, the minutes of their October 27-28 meeting showed on Wednesday.

Fed Governor Michael Barr said he's likely to support tighter monetary policy in an economy still beset by inflation pressures.

Additionally, Fed Governor Christopher Waller said the US central bank needs to respond more aggressively to inflation.

Markets see a 90% chance of a 25-basis-point US rate hike in December, while the probability of a larger 50-basis-point move is priced at 10%, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

Higher rates increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion, reducing its appeal to investors.

"The break below $3,800 risks reinforcing bearish sentiment. Buying interest remains subdued, while the continued decline raises the risk of further liquidation," analysts at OCBC said in a note.

Meanwhile, the global platinum market will swing back to deficit next year due to higher bar and coin demand and smaller outflows from platinum-backed exchange-traded funds, the World Platinum Investment Council said on Wednesday.

Spot silver rose 0.3% to $45.14 per ounce, platinum steadied at $1,370.6, and palladium gained 0.4% to $952.15.

data.title: The Iran War Could Permanently Slash Reliance on Hormuz, IEA Says
data.description:
(05:00 GMT) *Confidence in Strait of Hormuz Has Been Shattered During Iran War, IEA Says
(05:00 GMT) *IEA: Middle East Set to Remain Cornerstone of Global Oil, Gas Supply
(05:00 GMT) The Iran War Could Permanently Slash Reliance on Hormuz, IEA Says

By Giulia Petroni

Shipping disruptions due to the Iran war have shattered confidence in the Strait of Hormuz, spurring a costly overhaul of the global energy trade that could dramatically cut the world's dependence on the route over the next decade, the International Energy Agency said.

Before the conflict, around 20 million barrels of oil a day passed through Hormuz, a narrow waterway connecting the Persian Gulf to global markets. That could fall to 8.5 million barrels a day by 2030 and to less than 2 million by 2035 if the strait remains severely disrupted, the Paris-based agency said in its World Energy Outlook.

"The Hormuz crisis has delivered a huge shock to the system," IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol said. "I don't see any credible pathway for the energy world to return to the way it was before."

Still, the Middle East is set to remain the world's largest exporter of oil to international markets as major Gulf producers race to build alternative pipelines and routes.

Since the Iran war began in late February, Saudi Arabia has relied on its East-West pipeline to move crude toward the Red Sea, while the United Arab Emirates used its pipeline to the port of Fujairah on the Gulf of Oman.

Now, around 7 million barrels a day of new pipeline capacity is under construction or under consideration to help Gulf producers move oil without passing through the strait, the IEA said. Building the projects will require an estimated $40 billion of investment, adding about $2 to the cost of each barrel of Middle Eastern oil exported, the agency estimates.

"It is not easy, but the energy world could conceivably manage without the strait," Birol said. "It cannot manage without the Middle East."

Meanwhile, global oil prices have been volatile: Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, swung from around $71 a barrel prewar to peaks above $126, before falling back toward $93 a barrel in November.

The price reaction was less severe than the scale of the disruption might have suggested, coinciding with a time of ample global supply and well-stocked inventories.

The IEA now expects the global oil market to swing back into oversupply as Middle Eastern production recovers faster than global demand growth. From a surplus of 1.7 million barrels a day in the current quarter, the glut is set to widen further next year to about 3.8 million barrels a day.

Between March and October, global oil demand fell by around 3.7 million barrels a day from a year earlier, as higher prices, physical shortages, government-imposed measures and weaker economic activity curbed consumption.

The decline was particularly sharp in the Middle East, where demand dropped 10%, and Asia, where it fell 5%. China's seaborne crude imports fell to around 6 million barrels a day in June from 11.6 million in February as the country drew down inventories, restricted fuel exports and switched between fuels.

Over time, the IEA also expects the crisis to reinforce a broader shift toward countries' domestic energy sources. Renewables and nuclear energy will be the biggest beneficiaries, while energy-efficiency measures, biofuels and, in some Asian countries, coal could also gain ground.

"All in all, countries want to rely more and more on homegrown energy," Birol said.

Volatile fuel prices have reinforced the case for electrification. Global demand for electricity has grown faster than the world economy since 2019 and at twice the rate of overall energy demand, driven by electric vehicles, air conditioning, industrial motors, heat pumps and data centers. The IEA expects electricity demand to accelerate further through 2035, with electricity approaching 30% of final energy consumption across all scenarios.

In its World Energy Outlook, the IEA presents a series of possible scenarios rather than a single forecast.

Write to Giulia Petroni at giulia.petroni@wsj.com

data.title: Korean Entertainment Stocks Surge on Hopes of K-Pop's Return to China
data.description:
By Megan Cheah

Shares of South Korean entertainment companies rose sharply after Seoul's agreement with Beijing opened the door for China to potentially loosen rules barring major K-pop acts from performing in the country.

South Korean President Lee Jae Myung and China's leader Xi Jinping on Wednesday signed a bilateral free-trade agreement on services and investment, covering sectors such as film, during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China.

The deal suggests that China could be warming up to ending its de facto ban on Korean pop culture, sparking a rally in entertainment stocks.

Kospi constituent Hybe, the company managing boy band BTS, advanced 13% on Thursday. Shares of entertainment and media company CJ ENM, listed on the smaller Kosdaq board, climbed 23%. Television-drama producer Studio Dragon's stock jumped 30%, while K-pop company SM Entertainment gained 10%.

China's informal ban, which Beijing has never officially acknowledged, was imposed in protest of Seoul's decision to deploy a U.S. missile defense system in 2016. Since then, Chinese television networks, streaming platforms and movie theaters had effectively shut out Korean content, while major K-pop acts were largely barred from staging large-scale concerts.

The free-trade agreement has "revived hopes that Beijing will ease its restrictions on Korean entertainment," said Hana Securities analysts Lee Ki-hoon and Kim Chae-hyun in a note. K-pop companies' earnings could rise by around 40% if China eventually allows K-pop concerts to resume, they wrote.

Studio Dragon looks set to be a more direct beneficiary of the South Korea-China deal. "Studio Dragon could earn additional revenue if Chinese streaming platforms...begin airing Korean dramas they have already licensed, triggering revenue-sharing payments," the analysts said.

  • Jihye Lee contributed to this article.

Write to Megan Cheah at megan.cheah@wsj.com

data.title: Energy-security response to Iran war could cut oil demand by 4% by 2035, IEA says
data.description:
Key points:
  • IEA includes new stress tests for markets if Hormuz disruption continues
  • Conflict has caused cumulative losses of 2.8 billion barrels of oil and 60 bcm of gas, IEA says
  • Countries turning to electrification for energy security
  • Cooling demand in buildings will surpass heating for first time

By Susanna Twidale

The Middle East conflict has caused the biggest disruption ever to global oil and gas trade and could cut world oil demand by more than 4% by 2035 if governments accelerate electrification, efficiency and fuel-switching measures in response, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Thursday.

Energy markets have been rattled this year by the conflict, which has curbed shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, a route that typically carries about a fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas supplies and is a key artery for Gulf exports.

"In my view, the energy world will never be the same again as it was before the Iran war," IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol said in an interview alongside the release of the agency's World Energy Outlook 2026.

The conflict has resulted in cumulative losses of 2.8 billion barrels of oil and 60 billion cubic metres (bcm) of gas supplies from the Gulf, the Paris-based agency said.

The annual outlook includes a range of scenarios based on existing and proposed energy policies. This year it also examines how governments and markets could respond to prolonged disruption in Hormuz.

Under a new Additional Response Case (ARC), the IEA said energy security concerns could speed up electrification, energy-efficiency measures and efforts to reduce dependence on imported fossil fuels.

In that case, global oil demand in 2035 is 4.4 million barrels per day lower than under the agency's Stated Policies Scenario (STEPS), which reflects governments' current policy intentions. Electric vehicles alone would displace more than 11 million bpd of oil demand.

Global oil demand falls to 97 million bpd in 2035 and 85 million bpd by 2050 under ARC, compared with just over 101 million bpd in 2035 under STEPS

Gas demand under ARC is more than 300 bcm lower than under STEPS.

ELECTRIFICATION GROWING

The report said electrification is now cost-competitive across large parts of transport, heating and industry, although inadequate grids, charging networks and power supplies could slow its rollout.

"Many countries are seeing electrification as a policy option for energy security. Instead of importing energy, they decided to build energy at home," Birol said.

Electricity's share of final energy consumption is projected to approach 30% globally under STEPS, up from about 23% today, as transport, heating and parts of industry switch away from fossil fuels.

Alongside data centres, rising demand for cooling is emerging as one of the strongest drivers of electricity consumption. For the first time, demand for cooling in buildings has exceeded demand for heating, the IEA said, as higher temperatures and rising incomes drive rapid growth in air-conditioner use.
